- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.3) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative (sentiment < 0.2) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then drifts back toward historical mean — adjust for lagged momentum.
- When sentiment is rising (positive trend), model often overweights near-term momentum and ignores long-term structural trends.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates late-period price peaks (last 5–7 days) — apply upward bias correction for final 10–15 days.
- If sentiment is high and price is rising, model tends to forecast higher than true outcome — reduce forecast by 1–2% for high-sentiment upward trends.
- If sentiment is low and price is falling, model often undercorrects — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
